content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain spelt flour is made from the entire spelt grain after milling. Spelt is an ancient wheat species with a nutty flavor and a rich nutrient profile. The flour retains the bran and germ, making it high in fiber, protein, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spelt has been cultivated since ancient times and was a staple for the Egyptians and Romans.
Spelt flour contains a higher protein content than regular wheat flour.
It does contain gluten, but its gluten structure differs, so some people with mild wheat sensitivity tolerate it better.
Whole grain spelt flour keeps a natural golden hue and a distinctive nutty aroma.
Spelt is more tolerant of poor soil and climate conditions than common wheat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Spelt flour provides about 15 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and supports gut health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus, iron, zinc, and B‑vitamins essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Compared with refined wheat flour, spelt flour raises blood glucose more slowly.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Spelt contains phenolic compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Spelt flour contains gluten, so it must be avoided by people with celiac disease or severe gluten intolerance.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to spelt, manifesting as skin rashes or gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting grains before milling can mitigate this.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Whole grain spelt flour can be used in breads, rolls, pancakes, muffins, and cookies. It adds a subtle nutty note and a denser crumb. For lighter textures, blend part of the spelt flour with regular wheat flour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
